content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: shift the 09:45-10:15 breaks by 30 minutes and add IVR callbacks on both queues, at no extra cost, holding a predicted 85.7% service level against the 80% target.","why":"General is short because of a sick wave: 9 unplanned absences against a usual 2.4, leaving 51 agents against 57.6 expected. Demand and handle time are close to plan, so this is a staffing problem, not a volume one. P1 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and meets the target over the 09:45-15:30 window. It predicts 84.2% on general and 86.9% on payments, with abandons at 3.0%. Doing nothing (P0) would also just clear the target at 85.6%, so P1 is a small, free safety margin rather than a rescue. The prediction rests on only one interval of data so far.","trade_offs":["P1 vs P0: both cost nothing. P1 lifts general from 83.8% to 84.2% and cuts abandons from 3.2% to 3.0%. Rest-of-day service level dips slightly, from 90.1% to 89.9%, because the breaks are pushed later.","P2 (INR 4,320) uses overtime on general. It raises the window to 89.7% (general 91.3%) and cuts abandons to 2.2%, giving much more headroom if absences keep rising.","P3 (INR 4,680) adds overtime on payments as well. It reaches 90.5% overall and 91.0% on payments, and is the best protection if payments' high absence (6 against a usual 2.6) starts to bite.","P1 changes nothing on payments' service level (86.9%, same as no action), so payments has no extra cover if its absences worsen."],"watch":"General's service level in the next few intervals: the margin over 80% is only about 4 points. Also watch payments absence and service level. If either queue trends toward 80%, move to P2, or to P3 if payments is slipping too."}
